guide: This is a feedback loop that sends bugs and user feedback from your app to you automatically, so you fix problems without having to remember to check. You need a live app, an error-monitoring tool, a feedback form and a messaging app.
1. Add an error-monitoring tool such as Sentry to your app so crashes and bugs are recorded as they happen.
1. Add a simple feedback form or button inside the app, or a shared inbox, where users can report problems or ideas.
1. Create a Telegram bot with BotFather and note its token and your chat ID.
1. Use an automation tool such as n8n or Zapier, or a small Vercel serverless function, to receive each new error alert and feedback message.
1. Have that automation send you a Telegram message containing what happened, where it happened and a link to the details.
1. Log every item in a Notion database with a status column such as New, Fixing and Done.
1. Review the database once a week and fix the most frequent or most serious item first.
1. Apply the same idea outside work: write down the inputs you control (for example food and training) and measure them, so the results become predictable.
Watch out: Keep the token and keys in environment variables rather than in your code, and send alerts only for new or repeated problems so the messages stay useful and you do not start ignoring them.

```
You are helping me build a small feedback and bug-alert system for my app. I am not a developer by trade, so explain each step briefly and give me copy-and-paste code.
My app is <describe app and tech stack>. I have accounts with <Sentry or another error-monitoring tool>, <Telegram>, <Notion>, and <Vercel, n8n or Zapier>.
Build this flow:
1. Capture errors from the app using <error-monitoring tool> and add a simple in-app feedback form for users.
2. Send every new error and every feedback submission to a webhook that I host on <Vercel, n8n or Zapier>.
3. From that webhook, post a short Telegram message to my chat with what happened, where it happened and a link to the details.
4. Also add a row to a Notion database with the date, source (error or feedback), summary, link and a status of New.
Constraints:
- Keep all tokens and keys in environment variables, never in the code.
- Do not send duplicate alerts for the same error within an hour.
- Keep it as simple as possible, with no extra features.
Return: a step-by-step setup list, all the code and workflow configuration I need, the Notion database properties to create, and a quick way to test that each alert arrives.
```
